## A VLA is a vision-language model that outputs robot actions

- One network: pixels and language in, motor commands out
- Trained by imitation on human teleoperation demonstrations
- The de facto recipe for robot foundation models since 2023

## A world model learns what happens next

- Predict the future, given the present and an action
- Act by imagining rollouts before moving: the Dreamer lineage, 2019 onward
- The complement of a policy: it learns dynamics, not behavior

## Three families of world models

| Family | Exemplars | What it gives you |
|--------|-----------|-------------------|
| Latent dynamics | Dreamer | imagination for planning and RL |
| Video generation | Genie, Cosmos | promptable, general visual worlds |
| Neural simulators | DreamDojo, GE-Sim | action-conditioned rollouts for robots |

## Two paradigms, one team

|  | DreamZero | DreamDojo |
|--|-----------|-----------|
| Direction | inverse: video to action | forward: action to video |
| The product | a zero-shot policy | a neural simulator |
| Training data | 500 h of robot data | 44,000 h of human video |
| Its job | acts | imagines |

::: {.footnote}
Both NVIDIA, February 2026. The two halves of one loop.

## A WAM denoises video and action together

- One diffusion process over future frames and future actions
- Human video is no longer pretraining: it is action supervision
- DreamZero named the category: "World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies"

## Where does action supervision come from?

{{< video-card lapa-teaser >}}

- Inverse dynamics models label raw video with pseudo-actions
- LAPA (2024): learn latent actions from human video, no robot labels at all

## From two stages to one joint model

- 2024: a video model plus a separate action decoder, trained apart
- 2026: one transformer denoises frames and actions jointly
- Imagination becomes optional at inference: run the action pathway alone

## The architecture consolidated in 2026

| Style | Idea | Exemplar |
|-------|------|----------|
| Joint denoising | one flow over video and action | DreamZero |
| Interleaved mixture | mixture-of-transformers over frames and actions | Dyna-2 |
| Latent world + decoder | imagine in latent space, decode actions | LAPA lineage |

::: {.footnote}
The 2026 tutorial line: imagination is training-time scaffolding; at inference, recent WAMs skip video generation and act at VLA-class latency.
:::

## The race is for hours, not parameters

| Who | Hours | What |
|-----|-------|------|
| Dyna Robotics | 1,000,000 h | human egocentric video, zero robot data |
| Generalist AI | 500,000+ h | real-robot manipulation, about 9,000 end-effectors |
| Lightwheel EgoSuite | 100,000 h, open | egocentric human video, commercial use allowed |
| Amazon ABC-130K | 3,553 h, open | 134,806 bimanual teleoperation episodes |
| China, WRC 2026 | "90 data factories" | and, per the same panel, still not enough |

::: {.footnote}
The counterweight, Jul 2026: $\log N \propto 1/(P-c)$. Precision is the one axis data volume does not buy.
:::

## Five architectures, one scoreboard

| Architecture | Scales on | Actions come from | August 2026 signal |
|--------------|-----------|-------------------|--------------------|
| VLA | teleop demos | imitation head | &pi;0.5: RoboArena Elo 1622 |
| VLA + WM | demos + video | imitation, WM-guided | &pi;0.7 visual subgoals |
| World model | video | none: it imagines | real-time neural simulators |
| WAM | egocentric video | joint denoising | DreamZero: Elo 1750 |
| Hybrid | everything | both pathways | the predicted winner |

::: {.footnote}
NVIDIA, Jun 2026: WAM action tuning about 9 ZFLOPs, full video pretraining 50+, small VLA paths 7 to 10; inference 3 to 4x slower, closing. Their call: a hybrid wins.
:::

## A1. Dyna-2: the scaling law in detail

- 1k to 1M hours in nested subsets: one power law, four scales
- 14-task average success: 20%, 28%, 45%, 53%
- Cross-embodiment transfer emerges between 10k and 100k hours
- Distilled sampler: 10,203 ms to 110 ms, about 90x, one H100

## A2. Dyna-2: deployment and infrastructure

- Head-to-head vs DYNA-1, its VLA twin, same data: 65% win rate
- New-site zero-shot deployment: 87% vs 46%
- Bottle caps: about 10 minutes of data, success from 10% to 50%
- Ingestion 31x faster, 1M hours in under 3 weeks; roadmap 10M

## A3. RoboTTT: the mechanism

- TTT fast-weight layers in GR00T N1.7: 538M to 690M params
- 8K-timestep context at constant per-step latency
- Assembly: 79% vs 42%; one-shot human video: 6/10 vs 0/10
- Bimanual YAM arms; egocentric human video in the mix

## A4. GEN-1.5: lineage and evidence

- GEN-0 to GEN-1 to GEN-1.5, three releases in nine months
- One-shot 59% (±10); few-shot 83% (±9) after 10 gradient steps
- Those ten steps move the weights by less than 0.15%
- Composed prompts interpolate: regrasping and recovery emerge

## A5. Skild S1: ground-up in-context learning

::: {.two-up}
{{< video-card skild-s1-pancakes-prompt >}}

{{< video-card skild-s1-pancake-recovery >}}

- Pretraining scaled 1k to 100k h; the VLA degrades up to 3x more at L5

## A6. Zero-WAM and the academic lineage

- HumanGen: 74.2K human-robot pairs across 8.6K tasks
- RoboTwin 2.0 held-out suite: 47.0%, +29.5 pp over LingBot-VA
- BPP (Stanford): task diversity, not hours, drives ICL ability
- MimicDroid (UT Austin, ICRA 2026): the earlier academic thread

## A7. The data race: sources and fine print

- EgoSuite-Open100K: 90k + 10k h, LeRobot v3, about 27x Ego4D
- ABC-130K: 3,553 h, 134,806 episodes, bimanual YAM, fully open
- UBTech: a 566M CNY order reported at WRC 2026
- Curse of Precision: $\log N \propto 1/(P-c)$, resists data scale
